title: Hailee Steinfeld Officially Returns as Kate Bishop in Avengers: Doomsday
excerpt:
Marvel has confirmed Hailee Steinfeld will reprise Kate Bishop in Avengers: Doomsday.
The announcement came through a playful promotional video for Disney's Hexed.
body_md:
Marvel Studios and Disney Animation have provided a direct confirmation of Hailee Steinfeld's return to the Marvel Cinematic Universe. In a joint Instagram video published Sunday, the actress appeared to promote the animated film Hexed before the conversation took an unexpected turn toward Avengers: Doomsday. Unlike the many casting rumors surrounding the upcoming crossover, this announcement came from the companies involved.

Steinfeld begins the clip by explaining that she is there for Hexed, then jokes that a chair from a different production seems to have arrived. The camera reveals a black director's chair bearing her name. The accompanying caption explicitly invites audiences to see Steinfeld in Disney's Hexed before she returns in Avengers: Doomsday. The unusual crossover promotion makes the confirmation both playful and unmistakable.

The actress introduced Kate Bishop to live-action audiences in the 2021 Disney+ series Hawkeye, opposite Jeremy Renner's Clint Barton. Her character brought determination, archery skills, and a younger perspective to a franchise filled with established superheroes. She later appeared in the 2023 film The Marvels, a brief return that encouraged discussion about where Marvel might take its next generation of heroes.

Steinfeld has previously described Kate as an inspiring character because of her ambition, discipline, and willingness to pursue difficult goals. Those qualities help explain why the role has resonated with viewers. Nevertheless, the announcement does not establish how much screen time Kate will receive in Doomsday, which characters she will work alongside, or what part she will play in the central conflict.

The same report also discusses another recently confirmed return: Elizabeth Olsen's Wanda Maximoff. According to its account of the VisionQuest finale, an extension of a scene from Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness shows Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom moving rubble away from Wanda and speaking to her. That development is distinct from the Kate Bishop announcement, and it does not establish any direct story connection between the two characters.

Avengers: Doomsday is scheduled for theatrical release on December 18, 2026. Steinfeld's participation is now confirmed, but theories about a formal young-heroes team, her place in the final confrontation, or specific alliances remain speculation. The distinction matters: Marvel has identified another returning performer without revealing the shape of her story.
